name: DashMap (sharded RwLock hash map)
baseline: RwLock<HashMap> (parking_lot RwLock around std HashMap in the measurements)
verdict_reason: Under contention DashMap beats a single-lock map by large factors: 7.5x on a read-heavy mix at 16 threads and about 20x on an insert/remove-heavy mix at 8 threads. On one thread it is slower than RwLock<HashMap> (0.72x and 0.49x on two CPUs).
tier_reason: Independent results (leapfrog's fork of conc-map-bench) with public code, CPU and OS, and LTO/codegen-units flags stated.
claimed_speedup: Read-heavy, FxHash, Ryzen 9 3950X: 87.5 vs 11.7 Mops/s at 16 threads (about 7.5x, derived from page data) but 14.1 vs 19.4 at 1 thread; Apple M2 Max: 42.2 vs 3.4 at 12 threads (about 12x, derived from page data), 10.4 vs 21.2 at 1 thread. Exchange mix with SipHash at 8 threads: 26233769.293655325 vs 1331625.593635424 ops/s (about 20x, derived from page data).
workload: bustle harness (port of the libcuckoo benchmark) with u64 keys: read-heavy (98% reads, 1% insert, 1% remove) and exchange (10% read, 40% insert, 40% remove, 10% update).
hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 3950X (16 cores); Apple M2 Max (12 cores)
toolchain: nightly Rust (2022), lto = true, codegen-units = 1; dashmap 5.0
one_liner: Sharded concurrent HashMap with a HashMap-like &self API; scales far past RwLock<HashMap> under contention but is slower single-threaded.
how_it_is_fast: DashMap splits the table into many shards, each a hashbrown table behind its own RwLock, chosen by key hash. Threads touching different shards do not contend, so lock cache-line traffic is spread out instead of concentrated on one lock.
use_it_when: Many threads read and write a shared map and a single RwLock<HashMap> shows contention.
Write-heavy or mixed workloads, where its sharded locks held up far better than flurry and evmap in the same runs.
skip_it_when: Access is mostly single-threaded: RwLock<HashMap> was faster on one thread.
You hold a Ref or RefMut across other map calls or .await points: a second lock on the same shard deadlocks.
caveats: Measured with dashmap 5.0 in 2022; current releases are 6.x.
The baseline used parking_lot's RwLock, not std's; std's RwLock moved to futexes on Linux in Rust 1.62 (2022), after this run.
The read-heavy table used FxHash for every map; the exchange numbers use SipHash.
dashmap's own README points to conc-map-bench, which is run by dashmap's author and whose 2024 results omit an RwLock<HashMap> baseline.
tradeoffs: Readers still take shard locks, so a slow writer blocks readers of that shard.
Iteration locks shards one at a time and is not a consistent snapshot.
